subject: design/installer-without-browser-review
statement: Pyxis ships as an **atomic system release** — one tag builds every engine binary for every supported platform from one commit, packs one self-contained payload, and emits a build-derived **release manifest** that pins every artifact by hash and ownership class; an operand's config pins exactly the system version and the manifest hash (`design-brainstorm:installer-tech-design#D-1`). The release is consumed through **`pyxis`, the front-door orchestrator**: one binary owning init, converge/repair, doctor, and the single acquisition-and-execution path — `pyxis exec <tool> -- <argv>` — behind which every skill, hook, and CI line in an installed repo invokes the engine (`#D-2`). Acquisition is **lazy and per-exec-verified**: every execution re-hashes the cached binary against the manifest before running it, cache misses fetch-verify atomically, and `pyxis converge` pre-warms the full tool set so the offline floor holds (`#D-3`). Install, re-run/repair, and (later) upgrade are one converge over ownership classes; the bootstrap shim that fetches `pyxis` itself is the one shell first-mover, minimized and drilled.
